title: Exact learning for sparse spectra
statement: Let $n,k\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ have at most $2^{k+1}$ nonzero Fourier coefficients. Every hypothesis returned with positive probability by the exact sparse spectrum learning program on target $f$ agrees with $f$ at every input; in particular, its relative Hamming distance from $f$ is zero.
hypotheses_covered: The target has at most $2^{k+1}$ nonzero Fourier coefficients
The outcome lies in the support of the learner's output-and-cost distribution on the target
